public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Particular values of the Riemann zeta function

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Particular_values_of_the_Riemann_zeta_function)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace RiemannZetaValues

/--
$\zeta(5)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_five : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 5 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(7)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_seven : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 7 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(9)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_nine : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 9 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(11)$ is irrational.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_eleven : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 11 = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(2n + 1)$ is irrational for any $n\in\mathbb{N}^{+}$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_odd (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) :
    ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta (2 * n + 1) = x := by
  sorry

/--
$\zeta(3)$ is irrational.

[Ap79] Apéry, R. (1979). _Irrationalité de ζ(2) et ζ(3)_. Astérisque. 61: 11–13.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem irrational_three : ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta 3 = x := by
  sorry

/--
There are infinitely many $\zeta(2n + 1)$, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, that are irrational.

[Ri00] Rivoal, T. (2000). _La fonction zeta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs_. Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I. 331 (4): 267–270.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem infinite_irrational_at_odd :
    { n : ℕ | ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta (2 * n + 1) = x }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
At least one of $\zeta(5), \zeta(7), \zeta(9)$ or $\zeta(11)$ is irrational.

[Zu01]  W. Zudilin (2001). _One of the numbers ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational_. Russ. Math. Surv. 56 (4): 774–776.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11 33]
theorem exists_irrational_of_five_seven_nine_eleven :
    {5, 7, 9, 11} ∩ { a | ∃ x, Irrational x ∧ riemannZeta a = x} |>.Nonempty := by
  sorry

end RiemannZetaValues

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts infinitude of qualifying indices n : ℕ, including n = 0, whereas Rivoal's result concerns infinitely many irrational values ζ(2n+1) for n ≥ 1.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Removing the single index 0 does not affect infinitude, regardless of Mathlib's assigned value for ζ(1). For positive n, ζ(2n+1) is real, and these values are distinct: termwise comparison of the convergent Dirichlet series proves strict decrease at integer arguments greater than one. Thus infinitely many qualifying positive indices is equivalent to infinitely many distinct irrational values. The full ↔ was proved independently in /workspace/review/full_checks.lean.

sources_consulted: T. Rivoal (2000), La fonction zeta de Riemann prend une infinité de valeurs irrationnelles aux entiers impairs, abstract and Theorem 1; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0008051
R. Apéry (1979), Irrationalité de ζ(2) et ζ(3), Astérisque 61, 11–13; https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1979__61__11_0.pdf
review.notes: Checked all eight declarations. The existential real witnesses express ordinary irrationality of the zeta values; their equivalence to irrationality of the usual real Dirichlet series was proved in Lean. The positive-index hypothesis excludes the pole in irrational_odd, and its smallest allowed index gives ζ(3). The four-element complex-set intersection was proved equivalent to the intended four-way disjunction. All successful checks in /workspace/review/full_checks.lean are free of sorryAx and do not use the conjecture proofs. Zudilin's result was verified from the explicit statement in the cited Wikipedia article; attempts to read its original PDF did not yield usable text.
